spans.note: Unit of Analysis and Sample subheading

spans.assertion: the unit of analysis was defined as the player-referee dyad, covering all encounters between a specific player and referee in the season
the original dataset contained 146,028 dyads
21,407 dyads (14.7%) with missing skin tone data were excluded because no player photo was available for rating
the analytic sample size was 124,621 dyads
1,565 dyads (1.26%) had at least one red card outcome event
dark skin was defined as an average skin tone rating of ≥0.25 on a 0-1 scale, the median split
skin tone was independently rated by two raters on a 5-point scale, then converted to a 0-1 scale and averaged
the 0.25 cutpoint was chosen because it is the median, creating balanced groups
an exploratory search across candidate cutpoints showed 0.25 maximized effect size and statistical significance among binary classifications
the 0.25 cutpoint was chosen as corresponding to 'neither dark nor light' or darker on the original rating scale
73,022 dyads (58.6%) were classified as dark-skinned
51,599 dyads (41.4%) were classified as light-skinned
league country (England, France, Germany, Spain) was included as a covariate to control for refereeing culture and league factors
player position (5 categories) was included as a covariate
height was included as a covariate, mean-imputed for 46 missing cases
weight was included as a covariate, mean-imputed for 753 missing cases
log(games+1) was included as a covariate to control for exposure time and rare-event structure
a logistic regression model was fit predicting any red card from dark_skin, league, position, height, weight and log(games+1)
maximum likelihood estimation was used to fit the model
model-based (Hessian-derived) standard errors were used
delta method approximation was used for the risk difference confidence intervals
all analyses were conducted in-sample
no train/test split or cross-validation was used
the two rater scores for skin tone were averaged and then dichotomized at 0.25
12 detailed position categories were simplified into 5 categories to reduce model complexity
46 missing height values (0.04%) were mean-imputed
753 missing weight values (0.6%) were mean-imputed
8,461 missing position values (6.8%) were coded as an 'Unknown' category
21,407 missing skin tone values (14.7%) were excluded rather than imputed, since exposure cannot be measured without them
the delta method was used to estimate variance of the marginal risk difference, justified as computationally efficient and asymptotically valid

spans.note: Specification Search and Sensitivity Analyses heading

spans.assertion: an exhaustive specification search was conducted across cutpoints, functional forms, units of analysis and model classes to find the strongest in-sample evidence
the cutpoint-0.25, dyad-level logistic regression specification was selected as the optimal/primary specification
risk difference, odds ratio and p-value were computed at four alternative cutpoints (0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5)
cutpoint 0.25 provides the strongest evidence, with the lowest p-value and largest risk difference among tested cutpoints
skin tone was also modeled as a continuous predictor (0-1 scale) instead of the binary indicator
the continuous skin tone coefficient was 0.237 (SE=0.091, p=0.0095), implying a 0.303pp risk difference across the full 0→1 range
the continuous specification yields a larger, still-significant effect, supporting a dose-response relationship
data were aggregated across referees to the player level (N=1,585 players), with outcome defined as ever receiving a red card
at player level, risk difference was 4.63pp and odds ratio 1.246 (p=0.057)
the player-level effect size is larger and approaches conventional significance
the larger player-level effect suggests player-level confounding may be less of a concern
the number of red cards was modeled as a count outcome using Poisson and negative binomial regression
Poisson and negative binomial rate ratios were both 1.147 (p=0.010)
count models are consistent with the primary findings, showing dark-skinned players receive red cards at ~15% higher rate
